items.title: EU Artificial Intelligence Act — phased compliance implementation
items.summary: The EU AI Act establishes a risk-based framework for providers and deployers of AI systems. Obligations apply in phases and require classification, governance, documentation and monitoring appropriate to each use case.
items.financeImpact: Budget for compliance ownership, product controls, evidence retention and supplier assurance; reflect implementation costs and potential exposure in forecasts.
items.action: Maintain an AI-system inventory, assign each use case a regulatory role and risk tier, and track phased obligations with Legal and Product.

items.title: EU Data Act — cloud switching, data access and contract readiness
items.summary: The Data Act introduces harmonised rules on access to and use of data, switching between data-processing services, interoperability and safeguards for non-personal data.
items.financeImpact: Cloud-switching and contract requirements may affect supplier commitments, pricing, migration costs, customer terms and infrastructure concentration risk.
items.action: Review cloud and customer contracts, switching charges, data portability commitments and supplier exit plans with Legal and Engineering.

items.title: EU Pillar Two Directive — global minimum taxation readiness
items.summary: Directive (EU) 2022/2523 implements a global minimum level of taxation for in-scope multinational and large-scale domestic groups in the EU.
items.financeImpact: If the consolidated group meets the scope threshold, Finance needs jurisdictional data, effective-tax-rate calculations, top-up-tax forecasting and controlled reporting inputs.
items.action: Confirm group scope with the parent, document entity and data ownership, and maintain a Pillar Two calculation and filing calendar.

items.title: VAT in the Digital Age — digital reporting and e-invoicing transition
items.summary: The adopted VAT in the Digital Age package modernises EU VAT rules through digital reporting, e-invoicing and changes affecting platform and cross-border VAT administration.
items.financeImpact: ERP, invoicing, tax determination and reporting processes may require phased changes across EU registrations and transaction flows.
items.action: Map affected transactions and registrations, compare system capability with expected digital-reporting requirements, and build an implementation roadmap.
